question: Can an unchanged statutory formula acquire a new operative output because an official authority publishes a computed metric value?

governing_rule.metric_name: Total Number of Allowances in Circulation
governing_rule.publication_rule: The Commission publishes TNAC annually; the most recent published TNAC determines reserve placement or release under Article 1.

bands.quantity_rule: 100000000 allowances, or all remaining reserve allowances if fewer

downstream_effect.auction_supply_effect: Auction volumes are reduced to reflect the reserve placement.

source_observation_v0_1.reason: Can preserve official bytes but explicitly forbids inferring legal mutation from artifact observation alone and has no canonical metric-value semantics.

authoritative_dynamic_set_v0_1.reason: The legal input is a scalar computed metric, not member identity, membership or status in a set.

temporal_v0_1.reason: Can own publication/application dates but not the scalar observation, threshold band or arithmetic rule evaluation.

change_atom_v0_3.reason: A verified Change Atom requires at least one source textual mutation, but the governing formula is unchanged and the causal event is an official metric observation.

forbidden_inferences: Decision (EU) 2015/1814 Article 1 was textually amended by the 2026 TNAC publication.
TNAC is a member or status inside an authoritative dynamic set.
The TNAC publication date is the same thing as the September reserve-placement application start.
The Commission Communication is merely contextual metadata with no role in MSR operation.
A fake textual mutation should be manufactured to make Change Atom v0.3 accept the downstream effect.
The arithmetic result may be asserted without preserving both the official metric input and the governing formula.

official_sources.identifier: European Commission Market Stability Reserve page
official_sources.locator: Total number of allowances in circulation
190 494 202 allowances reflected in revised 2026 and 2027 auction calendars
